analysis.title: US Economic Weekly: Oct FOMC preview: Sea change or wee change?
key_insights: BofA keeps its call for a 25bp Fed hike at the Oct 28 FOMC, but acknowledges it would be a heavy lift given this week's price action. Conviction that the Fed should hike is strong, conviction that it will is low.
The large, broad-based beat in Sep inflation (CPI, PPI, import prices) offset last month's downward revisions and strengthens the case for an Oct hike. Core PCE could plausibly end 2026 at 3.4% y/y.
Markets price about a 10% chance of an Oct hike. Long-end yields are not questioning the Fed's inflation-fighting credibility, which gives the Fed a pass to hold.

The 10y yield has nearly fallen back below 5% and the ACM term premium is down over 25bp. This undercuts the argument that the bond sell-off is doing the Fed's tightening work, and a Fed that cited higher yields to justify caution but cites lower yields to justify caution again would show an asymmetric reaction function.

Staying on hold keeps the 'one and done' option and only makes sense if the Fed concludes the Sep hike was a mistake. Hiking in Oct keeps a Dec hike open and the cycle on the same cadence as the 2024-25 cuts. BofA thinks the second option is more valuable given most of the FOMC already backs two hikes this year.

Williams and Jefferson's forward guidance, delivered before the Sep data, led markets to price out an Oct hike. BofA says this cannot be squared with Chair Warsh's stated objection to forward guidance. A hike would signal the Fed has left coordinated messaging, while a hold risks Warsh losing relevance.

The Oct decision tests whether Warsh will bring a 'sea change' to Fed communication. Under Powell or Yellen there would be essentially zero chance of such a hawkish surprise, especially six days before the midterms. Warsh will have the votes either way.

If the Fed hikes, BofA expects no substantive changes to the statement. If it holds, the sentence 'Today's policy action will support a timelier return to the Committee's 2 percent goal' must be omitted or edited.

Press conference is expected to follow the Sep template, about 30 minutes with no follow-up questions. In a hike scenario, the risk is that Warsh sounds too hawkish and markets price an over-tightening policy mistake, producing a large risk-asset correction and twist-flattening of the curve. A 'midcycle adjustment' phrase could cap total hikes at 75-100bp.

In a hold scenario, Warsh must defend his prior line that 'inflation is a choice' and avoid sounding complacent. The risk is a repeat of the July presser: twist-steepening, weaker dollar and a moderate risk-asset selloff.
Outlook is little changed by an Oct hold: BofA still expects hikes in Dec '26 and Mar '27, with risk skewed toward more hikes (Jun '27, perhaps Sep '27) if y/y inflation stays sticky in 1H '27.

Sep core PCE is forecast at +0.3% m/m (0.35% unrounded) and 3.1% y/y, after upside surprises in CPI, PPI and import prices. Both core goods and core services accelerated. Headline PCE is forecast at +0.5% m/m and 3.7% y/y.

3Q GDP first print is forecast at an above-consensus 3.5% q/q saar, with consumer spending at 3.5% after 3.8% in 2Q. AI-related capex keeps business investment strong (equipment and IPP). BofA's mechanical tracking estimate is 3.7%, up one tenth after Sep industrial production.

Card spending per household was up 4.9% y/y in the week ending Oct 17 (3.7% ex gas). Gas spending was up 25.8% y/y. Furniture (-5.4%), department stores (-3.8%) and entertainment (-4.3%) were weak, airlines were up 9.1%.

Core views: 2026 growth 2.6% 4Q/4Q and 2027 growth 2.1%. Core PCE should finish 2026 slightly above 3% and fall to 2.5% in 2027. Job growth should average 70k/mo in '26 and about 60k in '27-'28 with the u-rate at 4.1% through 2027.

BofA's rate forecast has fed funds at 4.25-4.50% by Dec '26, a 2y yield of 5.00%, 10y of 5.00% and 30y of 5.25%, versus spot 2y 4.64%, 10y 4.95%, 30y 5.28%. USD-JPY is forecast to fall from 156.79 to 152 by Dec '26, EUR-USD to rise from 1.12 to 1.15.

Week ahead calendar: Sep durable goods, Aug home prices and Oct consumer confidence (Tue), advance goods trade (Wed), FOMC decision (Wed 2pm, press conference 2:30pm), Sep PCE and 3Q GDP (Thu), and 3Q ECI (Fri). The Fed blackout ends Thursday night, with Daly and Musalem scheduled Friday.

macro_indicators.interpretation: BofA is out of consensus. Market pricing implies roughly a 10% chance of an Oct hike. A hike would tighten financial conditions significantly, while a hold risks questions over Fed credibility.

risk_factors: Policy-error trade: if the Fed hikes, investors may worry about over-tightening, and if it holds, markets may question its inflation-fighting credibility.
Sticky y/y inflation in 1H '27 despite favorable base effects would push risks toward further hikes in Jun '27 and perhaps Sep '27.
Energy shock pass-through into core inflation, amplified by a strong nominal economy.
Risk assets have wobbled this week, which the Fed could cite as a reason to hike slowly.
Warsh's refusal to give forward guidance leaves the market vulnerable to guidance from other FOMC members, such as Williams and Jefferson.
charts_described: Exhibit 1: core PCE inflation with projections through end-2026 under a range of outcomes for Oct-Dec monthly prints, showing a plausible 3.4% y/y at year-end assuming Sep core PCE of 0.35% m/m.
Exhibit 2: ACM 10-year term premium, which has dropped over 25bp recently.
Exhibit 3: Fed hike pricing by meeting in bp, roughly consistent with three more hikes at a quarterly cadence.
vol_and_positioning: Fed hike pricing is about 10% for Oct and roughly consistent with three more hikes at a quarterly cadence.

Scenario risk: a hike with no forward guidance could cause a large risk-asset correction with twist-flattening of the curve. A hold could repeat the July presser reaction of twist-steepening, a weaker dollar and a moderate risk-asset selloff.
The 10y yield is near 5% and the 30y at 5.28%, while the 2y is at 4.64%.
geopolitical: The report attributes much of the current inflation overshoot to tariffs and the Iran war, and says the US economy remains resilient in the face of the energy shock.
Midterm elections are six days after the Oct 28 FOMC, cited as an added reason a hike would be an unusually large hawkish surprise.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case: Sep inflation beat was large and broad-based, core PCE could end 2026 at 3.4%, long-end yields have fallen so they no longer do the Fed's work, and a hike keeps the Dec option open and signals Warsh has exited coordinated messaging.
tension_points.bear_case: Hold case: markets price only about a 10% chance of a hike, the hike would come six days before the midterms, risk assets have wobbled and a hike without guidance could trigger an over-tightening policy-error trade. Fed speakers such as Bowman see no urgency.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hold at the Oct 28 FOMC would break BofA's out-of-consensus call, though BofA says it would still expect hikes in Dec '26 and Mar '27.

theme_stances.key_argument: Inflation is too high, the Sep beat was large and broad-based, and a hike keeps the Dec option open and shows Warsh has left forward guidance behind.
theme_stances.evidence: we maintain our out of consensus call that the Fed will hike two more times this year
